author: Henry James
title: The Turn of the Screw, in The Two Magics
edition: New York: The Macmillan Company; London: Macmillan & Co., Ltd., 1898. Scan-backed Wikisource transcription of this edition; chapter headings, navigation and page-number anchors omitted from prose excerpts; HTML line-wrapping whitespace collapsed. The library text holds the whole volume's fiction: The Turn of the Screw (the untitled prologue and Chapters I to XXIV) and Covering End (Chapters I to VIII), each under its printed title and chapter numerals; the title page, contents and publisher's advertisements are omitted. The Wikisource Covering End Chapter 7 page also transcludes the opening of Chapter VIII from the shared scan page; that repeated passage is kept once, under Chapter VIII. The Turn of the Screw, Chapters XI to XXIV, was collated on 2026-11-18 word by word against the OCR of Internet Archive twomagicsturnofs00jameiala (the scan behind the Wikisource transcription) and against Project Gutenberg 42486, each difference decided on the page images: the transcription had modernised that text, and fifty-six readings were changed to the print in forty-one paragraphs: word forms (“none the less” four times for “nonetheless”, “fulness”, “afterwards”, “unmistakeably”, “for ever”), hyphened compounds (“half-a-dozen”, “fairy-tale”, “break-down”, “out-of-doors”, “church-bells”, “house-door”, “mooring-place”, “half-way”, “tea-things”, “dressing-table”, “dining-room”, “wedding-journey”, “off-hand”), words (“elate”, “now permit”, “or of a discussion”, and “about”, “a feeling”, “and that now”, “a reference” restored), punctuation in twenty-two places, three long dashes, and one straight quotation mark made curly like the rest. The prologue and Chapters I to X (blocks 0 to 386, which the school nights read) were collated the same way on 2026-11-18, against the same OCR and Project Gutenberg 42486 with every difference decided on the page images, and showed the same modernisation: eighty-five readings were changed to the print in sixty-one paragraphs: word forms (“afterwards” five times, “favour”, “colour”, “rigour”, “learnt”, “recognised”, “recognise”, “practised”, “traveller”, “grey” three times, “curtsey”, “loveable” twice, “unmistakeable” once and “unmistakeably” twice, “none the less”, “dare say”), hyphened compounds (“Good-night”, “off-hand”, “see-saw”, “stopping-place”, “head-master” three times, “tea-time”, “bed-time”, “school-world”, “dining-room” three times, “ground-floor”, “far-away”, “window-seat”, “half-way”) and the unhyphened “half replaced and half utilised” and “half bowed”, words (“revolution”, “complication”, “turns”, “impression”, “facts”, “only a few seconds”, and “that” restored in “the revelation that left me”), “Miss” capitalised six times where Mrs. Grose addresses the governess, two long dashes, and punctuation in thirty-one places; twenty-five straight apostrophes were also made curly like the rest of the text. No printed misprint was found in either collated range. scope.collated records the text so collated, blocks 0 to 811: the whole of The Turn of the Screw, prologue to Chapter XXIV; Covering End (from block 812) has not been collated, and every reading of this work lies inside the collated range.

rights.basis: This 1898 English-language edition was published before 1931 and is in the US public domain as of 2026; only James’s narrative is supplied, with no modern annotation.

Only the transcluded scan text is used: Wikisource headers, page-number anchors and zero-width page-boundary characters removed (the transcription has no footnotes); the Covering End title page dropped; story titles and chapter numerals became headings; paragraphs joined with whitespace collapsed; emphasis flattened. On 2026-11-18 blocks 388 to 810 (The Turn of the Screw, Chapters XI to XXIV) were corrected in forty-one paragraphs, and blocks 2 to 386 (its prologue and Chapters I to X) in sixty-one, after collating them against the page images of IA twomagicsturnofs00jameiala, as the edition note records; no block was added, removed or split.
